g_add.label: Add
g_add.tooltip: Add two numbers. Use the second parameter to define what will be added with the variable value.

g_concatenate.label: Concatenate
g_concatenate.tooltip: Concatenate two strings. Use the second parameter to define what will be concatenated with the variable value.

g_addTimeSpan.label: Add Time
g_addTimeSpan.description: Add time span to a date.
g_addTimeSpan.tooltip: Add time span to a date.

g_avg.label: Avg
g_avg.description: Find the average (arithmetic mean) of given number(s).
g_avg.tooltip: Find the average (arithmetic mean) of given number(s).

g_ceil.label: Ceil
g_ceil.description: Round to the smallest integer greater than or equal to a given number.
g_ceil.tooltip: Round to the smallest integer greater than or equal to a given number.

g_condition.label: Condition
g_condition.description: Conditional statement. If EXPRESSION evaluates to true, TRUE VALUE branch will be the resulting value. Otherwise, FALSE VALUE will be used.
g_condition.tooltip: Conditional statement. If the value of the variable evaluates to true, the true value branch will become the resulting value. Otherwise, the false value will be used.

g_div.label: Div
g_div.tooltip: Divide two numbers. Use the second parameter to define the divider.

g_each.label: Each
g_each.description: Loop over all values of a list or an object.
g_each.tooltip: Loop over all values of a list or an object. For example, given a list ["John", "Mary"], we can output a string that will contain each name on a separate line by adding the "@value" (using the variable picker, i.e. "+" button) variable to the iteration, and an empty line character (just press enter after the "@value" variable in the iteration field.

g_filterList.label: Filter
g_filterList.description: Iterates over items in the list and returns a new list with values that pass the predicate.
g_filterList.tooltip: Loop over items in the list and return a new list with values that pass the predicate (i.e. the value parameter must evaluate to true).

g_equals.label: Equals
g_equals.description: Test equality of two values. Resulting value is true if FIRST EXPRESSION equals SECOND EXPRESSION.
g_equals.tooltip: Test equality of two values. Resulting value is true if the variable equals second expression.

g_first.label: First Item
g_first.description: Find the first item of a list.
g_first.tooltip: Get the first item of a list.

g_floor.label: Floor
g_floor.description: Round to the largest integer less than or equal to a given number.
g_floor.tooltip: Round to the largest integer less than or equal to a given number.

g_greaterThan.label: Greater than
g_greaterThan.description: Test if the first value is greater than the second value.
g_greaterThan.tooltip: Test if the variable is higher than the value provided in the second parameter. Set inclusive if you want to test for equality too.

g_greaterThanDate.label: Greater than
g_greaterThanDate.description: Test if the first date is greater than the second date.
g_greaterThanDate.tooltip: Test if the date in the variable is after the date in the second parameter. Set inclusive if you want to test for equality too.

g_pick.label: Pick
g_pick.description: Transforms the list by picking nested object values.
g_pick.tooltip: Transforms the list by picking nested object values. Use JSON Path (dot notation) to refer to nested values of the objects in the list. For example, given the list [{ "age": 30 }, { "age": 50 }] and using age as our JSON Path, the resulting list would become [30, 50].

g_map.label: Map
g_map.description: Create a new array by transforming items of the original array.
g_map.tooltip: Create a new array by transforming items of the original array. predicate is the function that will be applied to each item in the original array. This function can be, again, defined using (possibly nested) modifiers. Typically, you would add the "@value" variable using the variables picker next to the predicate field ("+" button) and apply other modifiers on the variable by clicking on the "@value" variable inside the predicate field. For example, given the list [{ "percent": 30 }, { "percent": 50 }], you can convert this to a list that looks like [0.3, 0.5] by adding the "@value" variable to the predicate field and applying the following modifiers to it in order: "JSON Path" (percent) and "Div" (100).

g_join.label: Join
g_join.tooltip: Create a new string by joining list of strings using a separator.

g_jsonPath.label: JSON Path
g_jsonPath.description: Access nested properties of the VALUE object using dot notation.
g_jsonPath.tooltip: Access nested properties of the variable object using JSON Path (dot notation). For example, if your variable is an object of the form { "invoice": { "amount": 50 } }, you can access the nested amount property by using the following path: invoice.amount.

g_last.label: Last Item
g_last.description: Find the last item of a list.
g_last.tooltip: Get the last item of a list.

g_nthIndex.label: Nth Index
g_nthIndex.description: Find the nth item of a list.
g_nthIndex.tooltip: Get the item of a list under the index specified.

g_initial.label: Initial
g_initial.description: Gets the first element(s) of an array.
g_initial.tooltip: Gets the first number of elements of a list. If no number is specified, it returns a list containing only the first item from the original list.

g_tail.label: Tail
g_tail.description: Gets all but the first element(s) of array.
g_tail.tooltip: Gets all but the first element of a list. If skip number is defined, it skips the defined number of items from the list (i.e. default is 1).

g_reverse.label: Reverse
g_reverse.description: Reverses array so that the first element becomes the last, the second element becomes the second to last, and so on.
g_reverse.tooltip: Reverses an array so that the first element becomes the last, the second element becomes the second to last, and so on.

g_flatten.label: Flatten
g_flatten.description: Flattens array a single level deep or recursively.
g_flatten.tooltip: Flattens an array a single level deep or recursively (if deep is set). For example, an array [1, [2, [3, [4]], 5]] is converted to [1, 2, [3, [4]], 5].

g_sum.label: Sum
g_sum.description: Calculates the sum of the values in an array.
g_sum.tooltip: Calculates the sum of the values in an array.

g_maxList.label: Max
g_maxList.description: Finds the maximum number in an array of numbers.
g_maxList.tooltip: Finds the maximum number in an array of numbers.

g_minList.label: Min
g_minList.description: Finds the minimum number in an array of numbers.
g_minList.tooltip: Finds the minimum number in an array of numbers.

g_avgList.label: Mean
g_avgList.description: Calculates the average of numbers in an array of numbers.
g_avgList.tooltip: Calculates the average of numbers in an array of numbers.

g_length.label: Length
g_length.description: Find length of text or list.
g_length.tooltip: Get the length of text or list.

g_lessThan.label: Less than
g_lessThan.description: Test if the first value is less than the second value.
g_lessThan.tooltip: Test if the variable is lower than the value provided in the second parameter. Set inclusive if you want to test for equality too.

g_formatDate.label: Format Date
g_formatDate.description: Format a date/time string using a string of tokens.
g_formatDate.tooltip: Format a date/time string using a string of tokens. For example dddd, MMMM Do YYYY, h:mm:ss a returns Sunday, February 14th 2010, 3:25:50 pm.

g_relativeTime.label: Relative Time
g_relativeTime.tooltip: Format a relative date/time. Example result 2 hours ago. Set without suffix to return only 2 hours.

g_lessThanDate.label: Less than
g_lessThanDate.description: Test if the first date is less than the second date.
g_lessThanDate.tooltip: Test if the date in the variable is before the date in the second parameter. Set inclusive if you want to test for equality too.

g_max.label: Max
g_max.tooltip: Find the maximum number in a list of numbers.

g_min.label: Min
g_min.tooltip: Find the minimum number in a list of numbers.

g_mod.label: Mod
g_mod.description: Calculate the remainder after division of one number by another.
g_mod.tooltip: Calculate the remainder after division of one number by another defined in the second parameter.

g_mul.label: Mul
g_mul.tooltip: Multiply two numbers. Use the second parameter to define the multiplier.

g_not.label: Not
g_not.description: Invert value. True value becomes false and vice versa.
g_not.tooltip: Invert value. True value becomes false and vice versa.

g_md5.label: MD5
g_md5.description: Gets an MD5 hash of the text.
g_md5.tooltip: Gets an MD5 hash of a text.

g_extractEmail.label: Extract Email Addresses
g_extractEmail.description: Returns a list of email addresses found in the text.
g_extractEmail.tooltip: Returns a list of email addresses found in the text.

g_extractUrls.label: Extract URLs
g_extractUrls.description: Returns a list of URLs found in the text.
g_extractUrls.tooltip: Returns a list of URLs found in the text.

g_encodeUrl.label: Encode URL
g_encodeUrl.description: Encode URL or a URL component.
g_encodeUrl.tooltip: Encode URL or a URL component by replacing each instance of certain characters by one, two, three, or four escape sequences representing the UTF-8 encoding of the character. For example, test? becomes test%3F.

g_decodeUrl.label: Decode URL
g_decodeUrl.description: Decode URL or a URL component.
g_decodeUrl.tooltip: Decode URL or a URL component. For example, test%3F becomes test?.

g_regex.label: Regex
g_regex.tooltip: Find matches using a regular expression. For example, given an HTML page as a string, we can extract the page title by using the following pattern: <title[^>]*>(.*?)</title>.

g_trim.label: Trim
g_trim.description: Removes leading and trailing whitespace or specified characters from string.
g_trim.tooltip: Removes leading and trailing whitespace or specified characters from string.

g_trimStart.label: Trim Start
g_trimStart.description: Removes leading whitespace or specified characters from string.
g_trimStart.tooltip: Removes leading whitespace or specified characters from string.

g_trimEnd.label: Trim End
g_trimEnd.description: Removes trailing whitespace or specified characters from string.
g_trimEnd.tooltip: Removes trailing whitespace or specified characters from string.

g_truncate.label: Truncate
g_truncate.description: Truncates text if it's longer than the given maximum text length. The last characters of the truncated text are replaced with the omission string which defaults to "...".
g_truncate.tooltip: Truncates text if it's longer than the given maximum text length. The last characters of the truncated text are replaced with the omission string which defaults to "...".

g_escapeHtml.label: Escape HTML
g_escapeHtml.description: Converts the characters "&", "<", ">", '"', and "'" in text to their corresponding HTML entities.
g_escapeHtml.tooltip: Converts the characters "&", "<", ">", '"', and "'" in text to their corresponding HTML entities.

g_splitWords.label: Extract Words
g_splitWords.description: Splits text into a list of its words.
g_splitWords.tooltip: Splits text into a list of its words.

g_splitByWhitespace.label: Split By Whitespace
g_splitByWhitespace.description: Split text into a list of words by chunks of whitespace.
g_splitByWhitespace.tooltip: Splits text into a list of words by chunks of whitespace.

g_replace.label: Replace
g_replace.description: Replace parts of text using regular expressions or text patterns.
g_replace.tooltip: Replace parts of text using regular expressions or text patterns.

g_pad.label: Padding
g_pad.description: Pads text on the left and right sides if it's shorter than a specified length.
g_pad.tooltip: Pads text on the left and right sides if it's shorter than a specified length.

g_stringify.label: Stringify
g_stringify.description: Convert an object or list to a JSON string.
g_stringify.tooltip: Convert an object or list to a JSON string. Optionally define the number of space characters to be used as indentation (space parameter), clamped to 10. If this is a string, the string is inserted before every nested object or array.

g_sub.label: Sub
g_sub.tooltip: Subtract two numbers. Use the second parameter to define what will be subtracted.

g_kebabCase.label: Kebab Case
g_kebabCase.description: Converts text to kebab case. (Example: "Foo Bar" -> "foo-bar")
g_kebabCase.tooltip: Converts text to kebab case. Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar".

g_camelCase.label: Camel Case
g_camelCase.description: Converts text to camel case. (Example: "Foo Bar" -> "fooBar")
g_camelCase.tooltip: Converts text to camel case. Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "fooBar".

g_sha1.label: SHA1
g_sha1.description: Hash a string using SHA1 algorithm.
g_sha1.tooltip: Hash a string using the SHA1 algorithm.

g_sha256.label: SHA256
g_sha256.description: Hash a string using SHA256 algorithm.
g_sha256.tooltip: Hash a string using the SHA256 algorithm.

g_sha512.label: SHA512
g_sha512.description: Hash a string using SHA512 algorithm.
g_sha512.tooltip: Hash a string using the SHA512 algorithm.

g_base64.label: Base64
g_base64.tooltip: Generate a Base64 representation of a string.

g_deduplicate.label: Deduplicate
g_deduplicate.description: Filter unique values or objects in an array if property name is provided.
g_deduplicate.tooltip: Filter out duplicate values of an array. If the items of the array are objects, you can filter by specifying the property.

g_snakeCase.label: Snake Case
g_snakeCase.description: Converts text to snake case. (Example: "Foo Bar" -> "foo_bar")
g_snakeCase.tooltip: Converts text to snake case. Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo_bar".

g_lowerFirst.label: Lower First
g_lowerFirst.description: Converts the first character of text to lower case.
g_lowerFirst.tooltip: Converts the first character of text to lower case.

g_upperFirst.label: Upper First
g_upperFirst.description: Converts the first character of text to upper case.
g_upperFirst.tooltip: Converts the first character of text to upper case.

g_javascript.label: JavaScript Function
g_javascript.description: Run JavaScript code to transform a variable.
g_javascript.tooltip: Run JavaScript code to transform a variable. Use $variable to reference the variable in your code. For example, to multiply a number by 5, type $variable * 5 to the code parameter. The code parameter supports multiple forms of the JavaScript code. All of the following will be evaluated correctly: return $variable * 5, function($variable) { return $variable * 5; }.
